sources_considered.why: Read the complete referenced essay to assess whether it specifies criteria.
An explicit earlier definition provides material context against reading the omission as never having specified criteria.
The original essay supplies its own account of general intelligence, but does not establish a change from its authors' earlier commitments.
Read the report. It describes a private contractual definition through another outlet's reporting; it does not establish that OpenAI replaced its public definition.
Read the charter. Its economic criterion alone cannot establish the sequence or purpose of an alleged change.

evidence_items.explanation: The complete essay discusses building AGI and its implications without restating a definition or test. This supports the narrow omission claim, while its reference to a traditional understanding leaves open an existing external definition.

receipt.public_excerpt: AI systems that are generally smarter than humans

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI had publicly stated an AGI definition before Reflections. That limits any inference from the later essay's omission to an absence of criteria altogether, but does not establish whether its criteria changed.

Agüera y Arcas and Norvig explicitly discuss criteria across topics, tasks, modalities, languages, and instructability. Their different conception of AGI does not by itself demonstrate a change from their own earlier criteria.

unresolved_gaps: A matched sequence establishing a material change in the same named actor's criteria was not established.
The sources do not establish deliberate evasion.
A private contractual threshold cannot automatically be treated as a replacement public definition.
